whoWeAre.title: Who is KAFA?
whoWeAre.description: COOPERATIVE INSURANCE FORCE OF HAITI (KAFA) is a cooperative insurance owned by its members. Its mission is to protect members against life's major challenges: death, illness, accidents, and other situations that can devastate a family's finances. KAFA always seeks to act in the best collective interest of its members, not in the interest of a single person.
whoWeAre.democracyDesc: each member has one vote in decisions, regardless of how many "social shares" they own
whoWeAre.mutualizationDesc: we pool all members' risks together for better management
whoWeAre.frenchNote: In French (summary): KAFA is a cooperative insurance company owned by its insured members, founded on solidarity, democracy and risk mutualization.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose KAFA?
whyChoose.subtitle: We understand how the death of a loved one can cause financial hardship for families. That's why we created KAFA to help you.
whyChoose.guaranteeDesc: We guarantee payment of all valid claims according to the contract.
whyChoose.affordableDesc: Plans adapted for all budgets, from 250,000 to 500,000 Gdes.
whyChoose.coverageDesc: Our services are available in all departments of Haiti.
whyChoose.fastDesc: We process claims quickly to relieve families.
whyChoose.noExamDesc: Some plans don't require a medical exam to register.
whyChoose.cooperativeDesc: You're not just a client, you're also an owner!

problemSolution.title: Problem and Solution
problemSolution.description: When a loved one dies, Haitian families often face major financial difficulties. That's why KAFA recognizes the urgency to act and provide a quick and appropriate response to families in difficult economic situations.

infoBlock.whoWeAreDesc: KAFA is an insurance company owned by its insured members. Its mission is to protect its members against risks and losses (death, illness, etc.). It exists to serve the collective interest of its members. KAFA operates according to principles of solidarity, democracy, and risk sharing. Each member has one vote in decision-making, regardless of the number of shares they own.
infoBlock.missionDesc: Offer accessible insurance services to all Haitians, to protect them from unforeseen events and prevent any loss of capital in case of sudden difficulties.
infoBlock.visionDesc: Become a reference in the insurance sector, while participating in building a more equitable society where everyone can live with confidence despite life's uncertainties.

policy.title: Conditions, Policy, and Privacy
policy.regulationDesc: Regulation on a funeral plan: This document defines the conditions, benefits and compensation methods related to an insurance contract covering funeral expenses. It ensures that the family or relatives of an insured can receive financial assistance to cover a good part of expenses before, during, and/or after the funeral.
policy.objectiveDesc: The funeral plan chosen by the insured aims to cover all or part of the expenses required for the funeral, in accordance with the established terms.
policy.beneficiariesDesc: KAFA will provide benefits to the beneficiary(ies) designated by the insured in case of their death.
policy.compensationIntro: The compensation terms are as follows:
policy.comp1: After completion of the first two years from the contract issue date, the beneficiary will receive 80% of the death benefit.
policy.comp2: From the third year, the beneficiary will receive 90% of the death benefit.
policy.comp3: From the fourth year, the benefit is fully covered (100%).
policy.comp4: However, if the insured dies before 2 years of KAFA membership, 85% of premiums received by KAFA will be refunded to the designated beneficiary.
policy.comp5: In case of death of the policy owner before the insured, the insured or another member must continue paying insurance premiums. However, if premiums are not regularly paid thereafter, insurance coverage will no longer be valid.
policy.coverageAmountDesc: The coverage amount provided by the funeral plan is set at subscription.
policy.premiumDesc: The insurance premium is the regular payment made to KAFA by the insured or owner to maintain an active insurance policy.
policy.gracePeriodDesc: A 30-day extension is granted to the insured after a premium due date during which the insured can still pay without losing coverage or incurring penalties and/or contract termination.
policy.nonPaymentDesc: In case of non-payment of a contribution at the insurance policy due date, coverage will be suspended 30 days after formal notice to the insured. If payment is not made within this period, the contract is terminated by operation of law.
policy.eligNote: Any subscription by a person aged between 65 and 80 must include at least one insured person under 65 years of age.
policy.uncoveredCostsDesc: Certain specific costs or benefits not covered such as travel expenses and/or personal belongings.
policy.uncoveredDeathsDesc: This contract excludes deaths due to acts of war, natural disasters, disappearance, pandemic, suicide, etc. (to be defined).
policy.requiredDocsDesc: In case of death, KAFA requires the original contract and the insured's death certificate.
policy.compensationDelayDesc: Compensation will be paid to the designated beneficiary within 7 to 14 business days.
policy.beneficiaryDesignationDesc: The insured can designate beneficiaries for the benefits.
policy.beneficiaryChangeDesc: Beneficiary change terms will only be modified in case of death or contract update. The insured can modify the clause by contract amendment, by will, or by letter addressed to KAFA.
policy.beneficiaryNote: The insured can change beneficiary if the latter is the insurance owner.
policy.section8Desc: The regulation defines the conditions under which the contract can be terminated, whether at the initiative of the insured or the insurer.
policy.section9Desc: Modifications may be made to this regulation if management deems it appropriate.
policy.importantNote: Specific details may vary, so it is essential to read the contract carefully to understand exactly what is covered and each party's obligations.

howToInvest.intro: You can invest in "KAFA" by purchasing preferred shares, which offer a competitive interest rate, in accordance with the terms and conditions established by the cooperative.

preferredShare.title: What Is a Preferred Share?
preferredShare.description: A preferred share is a participation certificate issued by a cooperative that grants its holder certain specific financial advantages over ordinary shares, within the limits set by the bylaws and applicable regulations.
preferredShare.advantage1: A priority return, in the form of interest or a preferred patronage refund, when the cooperative generates surpluses and their distribution is authorized.
preferredShare.advantage2: A preferential right to this return according to the terms provided by the bylaws or the share issuance conditions.
preferredShare.advantage3: A priority reimbursement of invested capital in the event of share buyback by the cooperative or upon its liquidation, subject to creditors' rights.
preferredShare.governance: However, holding preferred shares confers no advantages in terms of governance. The fundamental cooperative principle of "one person, one vote" remains fully applicable, regardless of the number or category of shares held by a member.

priorityReturn.title: Priority Return
priorityReturn.description: This means that holders of certain shares (preferred shares) have the right to receive a return (interest or dividend, depending on the legal framework) before holders of ordinary shares receive any return. This priority does not necessarily guarantee payment: it applies only if the cooperative has distributable profits and if distribution rules allow it.

patronageRefund.title: Preferred Patronage Refund
patronageRefund.description: In a cooperative, a patronage refund is a redistribution of surpluses to members based on their use of the cooperative (for example, their purchases, sales, or volume of business with the cooperative), and not based on the capital they have invested.
patronageRefund.preferred: A preferred patronage refund refers to a refund granted on a priority basis or under preferential conditions to certain holders of preferred shares, if the cooperative's bylaws or applicable law permit it.

parValue.title: Par Value (Nominal Value)
parValue.description: The par value is the value assigned to a share at the time of its issuance. It is a value set in the bylaws or by the resolution authorizing the issuance of shares; it does not necessarily correspond to the market value of the share.
parValue.usesTitle: In a cooperative, the par value is used notably to:
parValue.use1: Determine the issuance price of a share;
parValue.use3: Establish, in certain cases, the basis for calculating the return on shares (for example, an interest rate of 5% on the par value).
